title: Saw's $1M marketing month: attention stunts, one-tap booking and fighting card fraud
summary: A vlog from inside a 20-year-old founder's flight-booking startup during a heavy marketing push. Alex explains positioning against commoditized airlines, the one-tap Tesla analogy, spending investment money on attention stunts, and a fraud problem that came with sudden growth. The creator-sponsorship playbook is mostly described by his YouTube head, Nathan.

principles.text: In a commoditized market, win on experience even if margins shrink.
principles.quote: No one's innovated. Everyone's too scared to because the margins on flights, they're very low. They're commoditized, but like I see a world where even if we make less money, we can still be the best.

principles.text: Incumbents profit from friction and upsell confusion; removing it is your wedge.
principles.quote: Airline companies, they make money by confusing you with the upsells, the multiple pages. That's how they make money.

principles.text: Cut the purchase flow to the fewest taps, like Tesla did for online car buying.
principles.quote: It's just one tap, find the flight book, enter code, it's done.

principles.text: Monetize through small add-on fees and expand into adjacent categories rather than inflating prices.
principles.quote: If if we charge like a small fee on bags and seats and then maybe we get into hotels, I think we'll be we'll be fine.

principles.text: Spending investment money on attention-grabbing stunts is justified if it earns attention.
principles.quote: We spent some investment money on it. And hey, look, it it gets the attention. So, job well done.

principles.text: Fight fraud with targeted checks, not blanket country bans that would block legitimate customers.
principles.quote: can't just ban Acura because longterm someone's actually going to have a real flight from there and that's not good.
